issues.legal_issue: In an ejectment suit where the defendant admits the plaintiff’s title and claims to have received possession from the plaintiff as a tenant, the limitation rule based on dispossession or discontinuance applies only if such dispossession or discontinuance is alleged.
material_facts: The plaintiff asserted title and continued possession, and sought possession only in the alternative if he were deemed dispossessed because of criminal proceedings.
The defendants admitted the plaintiff’s title and claimed that the plaintiff had given them the land to cultivate as tenants, while also asserting occupancy rights.
Neither side alleged that the plaintiff had been dispossessed or had discontinued possession.
The defendants’ asserted settlement and possession were rejected by the appellate court.
issues.conclusion: Article 144, rather than Article 142 of the Indian Limitation Act, 1908, applied, and the suit was not barred by limitation.
issues.legal_principle: Under Articles 142 and 144 of the Indian Limitation Act, 1908, where a defendant admits the plaintiff’s title and admits deriving possession from the plaintiff as a tenant, the case proceeds on the defendant’s plea; for deciding which article applies, dispossession or discontinuance within Article 142 is not assumed when neither party alleges it. The Court approved Jaldhari v. Rajendra Singh, A.I.R. 1958 Pat. 386. It distinguished The Official Receiver of East Godavari v. Chava Govinda Raju, I.L.R. [1940] Mad. 953, and Behari Lal v. Sundar Das, I.L.R. (1935) 16 Lah. 442, where the defendant asserted an independent title. It also referred to Kumbham Lakshmanna v. Tangirala Venkateswarlu, (1948-49) L.R. 76 I.A. 202, Seturatnam Aiyar v. Venkatachala Gounden, (1919) L.R. 47 I.A. 76, and Nainapillai Marakayar v. Romanathan Chettiar, L.R. 51 I.A. 83, concerning the burden where tenants claim occupancy rights.

predicates.ejectment_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking recovery of land from persons in possession.
predicates.defendant_admits_plaintiff_title: The defendant admitted that the plaintiff held title to the land.
predicates.defendant_claims_possession_derived_as_t: The defendant claimed that the plaintiff had given the land to the defendant to cultivate as a tenant.
predicates.neither_side_alleges_dispossession_or_di: Neither party alleged that the plaintiff had been dispossessed or had discontinued possession.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff seeks ejectment, the defendant admits the plaintiff’s title and claims possession derived from the plaintiff as a tenant, and neither side alleges dispossession or discontinuance, the suit is not barred on that basis.

issues.legal_issue: When the record contains no finding that the plaintiff is in possession, a decree in a suit seeking confirmation of title and, alternatively, possession must be limited to possession.
material_facts: The plaintiff claimed title and possession, and sought a decree for possession in the alternative.
The Court found no determination by the courts below that the plaintiff was in possession.
issues.conclusion: The decree was modified and limited to a decree for possession of the disputed land.
issues.legal_principle: The Court limited the relief to possession because the courts below had made no finding that the plaintiff was in possession; the judgment states no separate statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this modification.

predicates.suit_seeking_title_confirmation_and_alte: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking confirmation of title and, alternatively, recovery of possession.
predicates.lower_courts_make_no_finding_of_plaintif: The lower courts made no finding that the plaintiff was in possession of the disputed land.

issues.definition: When a suit seeks confirmation of title and alternatively possession, and the lower courts made no finding that the plaintiff was in possession, the decree is limited to possession.
